title: Saturn's Vanishing Rings
subtitle: They're raining away
description:

segments.text: Episode eighty-two. Next stop... Saturn's vanishing rings.
Saturn's rings are one of the most beautiful sights in the solar system.
segments.headline: Saturn's rings

segments.text: They stretch hundreds of thousands of kilometers across, but in most places they're only about ten meters thick.
They're made almost entirely of water ice, from tiny grains to chunks as big as houses.
segments.headline: Made of ice

segments.text: But they won't last forever. Saturn's gravity and magnetic field are pulling ring material down into the planet.
segments.headline: Raining into Saturn

segments.text: Scientists call it ring rain. Enough ice to fill an Olympic swimming pool falls into Saturn about every half hour.
segments.headline: Ring rain

segments.text: At that rate, the rings could be largely gone in a few hundred million years.
Some scientists think the rings are young, maybe younger than the dinosaurs. Others think they're as old as Saturn. The debate continues.
segments.headline: Young or old?

segments.text: And every fifteen years or so, the rings seem to vanish from Earth's view, when we see them exactly edge-on. That happened in twenty twenty-five.
segments.headline: Edge-on, they vanish
